Relational / ORDBMS

PostgreSQL

1996
Pioneered by: Michael Stonebraker & PostgreSQL Global Development Group

PostgreSQL is an enterprise-class, open-source object-relational database system with more than 35 years of active development. Known as the 'Linux of Databases', Postgres is famed for rock-solid data integrity, extensibility (foreign data wrappers, custom data types, PostGIS, pgvector), and full ACID compliance. It handles complex analytical queries, transactional workloads, and JSON document structures with equal mastery.

Storage Engine:Heap Files (append-only MVCC) + Buffer Pool
Storage Model:Row-Oriented
Query Interface:SQL (ANSI compliant) + PL/pgSQL
Concurrency:MVCC (Snapshot Isolation & SSI)
ACID & Consistency:Full ACID (Snapshot Isolation, Serializable SSI via SIREAD locks)
P99 Latency Profile:< 1ms OLTP point reads | 5-50ms analytical aggregate
Architectural Highlights & Internals:
  • MVCC Architecture: Multi-Version Concurrency Control prevents read-write blocking by retaining row versions during transactions.
  • Unmatched Extensibility: Pluggable procedural languages, custom index types (B-Tree, Hash, GiST, SP-GiST, GIN, BRIN), and extensions like PostGIS and pgvector.
  • Reliable Write-Ahead Logging (WAL): Guarantees zero data loss with point-in-time recovery (PITR) and synchronous/asynchronous streaming replication.
  • Native Hybrid Semi-Structured Data: Fast binary JSON processing via JSONB with GIN indexing for document queries.

Async Modern IndexedDB Transaction 
// Open database with typed object store and secondary index
const request = indexedDB.open('OfflineAppDB', 2);

request.onupgradeneeded = (event) => {
  const db = event.target.result;
  const store = db.createObjectStore('documents', { keyPath: 'id' });
  store.createIndex('by_author', 'author', { unique: false });
  store.createIndex('by_created', 'createdAt', { unique: false });
};

request.onsuccess = (event) => {
  const db = event.target.result;
  const tx = db.transaction(['documents'], 'readwrite');
  const store = tx.objectStore('documents');
  
  store.put({ id: 'doc-404', author: 'guigo', title: 'DB Internals', createdAt: Date.now() });
  tx.oncomplete = () => console.log('Transaction committed safely to local disk!');
};

C LMDB Zero-Copy mmap() Transaction 
#include <lmdb.h>

MDB_env *env;
MDB_dbi dbi;
MDB_txn *txn;
MDB_val key, data;

mdb_env_create(&env);
mdb_env_set_mapsize(env, 10485760); // 10MB virtual address map
mdb_env_open(env, "./lmdb_store", 0, 0664);

// Zero-copy read transaction (runs concurrently with zero lock contention)
mdb_txn_begin(env, NULL, MDB_RDONLY, &txn);
mdb_dbi_open(txn, NULL, 0, &dbi);

key.mv_size = 4;
key.mv_data = "1001";
mdb_get(txn, dbi, &key, &data);

// data.mv_data points DIRECTLY into kernel page cache (zero copy)
printf("Record size: %zu bytes\n", data.mv_size);
mdb_txn_abort(txn);

In-Memory Graph Database

Memgraph

2016
Pioneered by: Dominik Tomicevic & Marko Budiselic

Memgraph is an open-source, in-memory graph database built in C++ for real-time streaming analytics. Engineered as a high-performance alternative to Neo4j, Memgraph connects directly to streaming platforms like Apache Kafka and Redpanda, running complex Cypher graph pattern matching, network analysis, and fraud detection algorithms in sub-milliseconds on live event data.

Storage Model:Labeled Property Graph (LPG) in RAM
Query Interface:openCypher Query Language
Concurrency:ACID Compliant (Multi-Version Concurrency Control)
ACID & Consistency:Full ACID transactions (Snapshot Isolation and Serializable MVCC)
P99 Latency Profile:< 1ms in-memory graph traversals in C++
Architectural Highlights & Internals:
  • In-Memory Performance in C++: Delivers microsecond query latencies and up to 100x faster graph traversals than disk-bound alternatives.
  • openCypher Compatibility: Fully compatible with openCypher query syntax, enabling seamless migration from Neo4j applications.
  • Native Kafka/Redpanda Streams: Attaches directly to streaming message brokers to execute graph algorithms on in-flight data.
  • MAGE Graph Algorithms: Memgraph Advanced Graph Extensions library provides real-time community detection, PageRank, and link prediction.

snippetCode:
-- Query high-cardinality IoT sensor fleet using standard SQL
SELECT 
    date_bin(INTERVAL '15 minutes', time) AS time_window,
    device_model,
    location_id,
    AVG(voltage) AS avg_voltage,
    MAX(temperature) AS max_temp
FROM "iot_sensors"
WHERE time >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
  AND firmware_version = 'v2.4.1'
GROUP BY time_window, device_model, location_id
ORDER BY time_window DESC;

    PRIMARY KEY (emp_id)
) WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING;

SELECT * FROM employee_salaries 
FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
WHERE emp_id = 42;
